item.title: Trojanized Claude Code, Vapor Panda ARTEX Campaign, and eMudhra Weak-Key Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Oct 15:00 → 30 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

4 real? Tracking exploitation and patching of eMudhra’s weak keys — Must Read

Cloudflare found that eMudhra’s publicly recoverable intermediate CA keys were used to forge certificates within hours of disclosure, though it has seen no evidence of interception against its network. Most modern browsers are patched, but many bots, legacy clients, and Android WebView instances still accept the compromised certificate chain and need updates.

  • eMudhra’s eight affected intermediate private keys could be recovered almost instantly from public certificates, enabling anyone to create certificates for any domain that unpatched clients without Certificate Transparency enforcement would accept.
  • Cloudflare patched its high-priority systems, including Pingora-based customer origin-facing proxies, beginning on October 19 and completed a source-code analysis within four hours to identify other affected systems.
  • After deploying logging on October 21, Cloudflare recorded about 22,000 attempted TLS handshakes using the weak eMudhra keys, including approximately 160 certificates whose listed domain names were unrelated to the requested site.
  • Cloudflare found no evidence that the weak keys had been used to intercept its connections, but observed forged certificates dated less than an hour after Mozilla’s bug report became public.
  • Probe results indicated that most up-to-date modern browsers were patched, while bots, older browsers, and 30–40% of embedded Android WebView clients continued to accept the compromised certificate chain.

Technologies: proxy, remote-access, browser, mobile-os, operating-system

Products: pingora, cloudflare-warp, cloudflare-tunnel, android-webview, google-chrome, macos, upki

Vendors: emudhra, cloudflare, mozilla, google, apple

Trojanized Claude Code Extension Delivered Persistent SSH Backdoor to Developer Machines — Must Read

A trojanized Anthropic Claude Code VS Code extension version 2.1.313 was distributed through Open-VSX and Cursor for about 11 hours, installing SSH backdoor persistence and a reverse tunnel on affected developer machines. Anyone who installed it should treat the host as compromised, remove persistence artifacts, reinstall a clean version, and rotate accessible credentials.

  • The Open-VSX release of Anthropic Claude Code extension version 2.1.313 contained a malicious loader in extension.js and was also distributed through Cursor's mirrored extension marketplace.
  • The malicious extension added an attacker-controlled SSH key, set up operating-system-specific persistence, opened a reverse SSH tunnel to 134.209.82.225, and sent host reconnaissance data over HTTP.
  • Cursor reported that up to 5,000 of its users received the trojanized version during an approximately 11-hour exposure window on October 29, 2026.
  • Removing the extension alone does not remove the persistence artifacts, so affected users should check for the svc-telemetry SSH key, remove persistence, and rotate credentials reachable from the machine.
  • Clean versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.314 were verified to contain none of the listed malicious indicators.

Technologies: package-registry, remote-access

Products: claude-code, visual-studio-code, open-vsx-registry, cursor-marketplace, dev-machine-guard

Vendors: anthropic, cursor, microsoft, open-vsx, stepsecurity

Florida warns that 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers leaked in financial aid site breach — Must Read

Florida’s Department of Education says a breach of its Student Financial Aid website exposed personal data, including Social Security numbers, for nearly 4.9 million financial-aid applicants. The site was taken offline while officials investigate, though aid disbursements and student financial assistance are not expected to be affected.

  • Florida’s Department of Education said it became aware on October 19 of a breach involving the Florida Student Financial Aid website.
  • The breach exposed information on nearly 5 million people who applied for financial aid in Florida, including names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, and Social Security numbers.
  • Florida took the financial aid website offline and said some other department websites and services could face temporary disruptions.
  • The department said student aid disbursements, tuition payments, scholarships, grants, and student loans would not be affected or delayed.
  • Florida said it is working with the Florida Digital Service and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, and urged affected people to monitor their credit reports and financial accounts.

Products: florida-student-financial-aid-website

Vendors: florida-department-of-education

Chinese Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX to Target Over 200 Organizations Worldwide — Must Read

CrowdStrike says China-linked Vapor Panda used the AI-powered ARTEX framework to scale intrusions against more than 200 organizations worldwide, including government, telecom, defense, semiconductor, and financial targets. The campaign combined autonomous agent-driven reconnaissance and lateral movement with established techniques to deploy malware, steal credentials, and compromise cloud, Active Directory, email, and VPN environments.

  • CrowdStrike attributed a campaign using the AI-powered ARTEX penetration-testing framework to the China-based intrusion group Vapor Panda, also known as VexatiousTemper and overlapping with Earth Estries.
  • Starting October 17, 2026, Vapor Panda used ARTEX to target more than 200 organizations globally, including foreign ministries, U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear, and financial organizations, and telecommunications providers.
  • CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation activity at nine organizations, where the attackers deployed BLOODALCHEMY, a ShadowPad derivative, and conducted credential spraying, network scanning, and reconnaissance.
  • ARTEX coordinated planner and worker agents using DeepSeek and an unidentified subscription-based commercial large language model, while a human operator directed activities such as writing web shells and extracting domain administrator passwords.
  • CrowdStrike also described newly documented China-linked groups Hollow Panda, Overcast Panda, Titan Panda, and Veiled Panda, including Overcast Panda's use of the FlowCloud backdoor and Titan Panda's exploitation of hard-coded IIS machine keys in Intapp Time Server.

Technologies: web-server

Products: artex, intapp-time-server, internet-information-services

Vendors: crowdstrike, deepseek, intapp, microsoft

TeamViewer Flaw Lets Remote Computers Attack Users Who Connect to Control Them — Should Read

TeamViewer fixed CVE-2026-111585 in version 15.83, a high-severity flaw that lets a malicious remote host crash—and potentially execute code on—the computer connecting to control it. Users should update TeamViewer clients, Portable, Android Remote Control, and Host installations immediately.

  • TeamViewer version 15.83 fixes CVE-2026-111585, a high-severity flaw affecting TeamViewer clients before that version.
  • A malicious or compromised computer being remotely controlled can crash the TeamViewer application on the computer used to connect to it.
  • The affected products include the TeamViewer Full Client on Windows, Linux, and macOS, TeamViewer Portable for Windows, and the Android Remote Control app.
  • Remedio demonstrated code execution on Windows by bypassing operating-system defenses, although its demonstration used a host-side stand-in to provide some attack data.
  • TeamViewer said it was unaware of attacks exploiting the flaw when the fix was published, and it provides no workaround other than updating.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: teamviewer-full-client, teamviewer-portable, teamviewer-remote-control, teamviewer-host, teamviewer-remote-management

Vendors: teamviewer, remedio

Trezor warns of suspected crypto-theft implant in hardware wallet — Should Read

Trezor warned that a Safe 5 wallet sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis may contain a cellular-enabled hardware implant capable of capturing and transmitting recovery phrases. Users who bought devices from CryptoBilis since March 2026 should stop using them and move funds to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase.

  • Trezor received a report that a Safe 5 wallet purchased from CryptoBilis through Tokopedia in Indonesia contained an extra circuit board with a cellular module and antenna.
  • Trezor has not yet received and examined the reported device, so it has not confirmed whether it contains a malicious implant.
  • The customer’s unconfirmed information indicates that the implant may be able to read information displayed on the wallet screen, including the recovery phrase, and transmit it over a mobile network.
  • Trezor stopped sales through CryptoBilis on October 9, 2026, after the reseller was implicated in a similar Ledger device implant incident.
  • Trezor advises customers not to use devices bought through CryptoBilis from March 2026 onward and to move funds to a newly created wallet with a new recovery phrase if they have already used one.

Products: trezor-safe-5

Vendors: trezor, cryptobilis, ledger

Introducing Censys Starter Subscriptions — Optional

Censys has launched revamped Starter subscriptions with a simplified one-credit-per-action model, increasing search value by roughly fourfold. Plans start at $79 per month and include daily free searches, rollover credits, collections, and expanded asset-tag limits.

  • Censys has changed its usage model so that lookups, standard searches, and advanced regex queries each cost one credit.
  • The Starter plan costs $79 per month and includes 500 monthly credits, two Collections, and 10 asset tags.
  • Starter Pro costs $599 per month and includes 4,000 monthly credits, four Collections, and 25 asset tags.
  • Every registered Censys user receives five free searches per day that do not use subscription credits.
  • Unused subscription credits roll over to the next monthly billing cycle.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: censys-starter, censys-starter-pro, censys-search, censys-core

Vendors: censys

item.title: Third-Party Compromises, Hardware Tampering, and Government-System Malware Drive Cybersecurity News
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Oct 11:00 → 30 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Binance hack: how a compromised developer laptop can lead to a $6.3 billion breach — Must Read

Binance says its $6.3 billion theft may have begun with a compromised DevOps laptop, though it later found additional breach points and has not reported a private-key leak. The incident illustrates how stolen developer credentials and session tokens can enable attackers to pivot into trusted withdrawal-signing infrastructure without stealing wallet keys.

  • Binance estimates the incident's total impact at about $6.3 billion and says it may have begun with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop.
  • Binance later said its investigation uncovered additional points of breach beyond the laptop, but did not provide details.
  • Binance says it has found no evidence so far that wallet private keys were leaked, and it says it will cover all losses.
  • The article explains that credentials and active login sessions on a developer laptop can let an attacker access internal systems and eventually reach a service trusted to submit withdrawals.
  • Aikido says it blocked nearly 500 malware attacks on developer devices in the prior week.

Technologies: edr, source-control, package-registry, cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration

Products: aikido-device-protection, visual-studio-code, github, npm, amazon-web-services, kubernetes, safe-wallet

Vendors: aikido, microsoft, github, npm, amazon-web-services, safe

British spy agency cannot account for thousands of data storage devices, watchdog says — Should Read

UK watchdog IPCO says GCHQ cannot account for thousands of removable storage devices that may hold sensitive surveillance data, citing inadequate tracking and slow investigation. The report also disclosed that flawed intelligence software led to a small number of innocent people being wrongly linked to terrorism and subjected to counterterrorism stops.

  • The UK Investigatory Powers Commissioner’s Office said GCHQ cannot account for thousands of removable storage devices, including USB sticks, external hard drives, compact discs, and memory cards.
  • IPCO said it was very concerned about the issue and disappointed by the time GCHQ took to investigate it, while GCHQ has acknowledged that its tracking system for registered removable media was not sufficiently robust.
  • Some missing devices may contain data collected under the Investigatory Powers Act, although the report does not allege that any device reached adversaries or other unauthorized people.
  • GCHQ has conducted an audit, updated its processes and tools, and told IPCO it has addressed the watchdog’s recommendations, but it remains unclear whether the audit determined how many items are actually lost.
  • The report also found that flawed GCHQ intelligence wrongly linked a small number of innocent people to terrorism-related criminality, leading to five counterterrorism stops at ports where devices were downloaded and biometric data collected.

Hackers target government Windows systems in Asia with new malware — Should Read

Kaspersky identified NetamLoader, a previously unknown malware likely used in a supply-chain intrusion against a customized Windows 10 deployment at an Asian government agency. The malware abuses legitimate Microsoft components to evade detection, disable security checks, and download additional payloads, though the attackers and full scope remain unknown.

  • Kaspersky discovered previously unknown malware called NetamLoader on one computer during the first half of 2026.
  • The malware appears tailored to a specialized Windows 10 version used exclusively by government organizations in Asia.
  • NetamLoader uses legitimate Microsoft-signed programs and Patch My PC components to run malicious code, evade security tools, and download additional programs.
  • The malware can interfere with Windows security scanning, delete files and system logs, collect information about infected computers, and communicate through encrypted connections.
  • Kaspersky could not attribute the activity to a known state-sponsored group, determine how the malware reached the system, or confirm that sensitive information was stolen.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10, patch-my-pc

Vendors: microsoft, kaspersky, patch-my-pc

Trezor Warns of Suspected Hardware Implant in One of Its Wallets Sold by CryptoBilis — Should Read

Trezor warned that a Safe 5 wallet sold by CryptoBilis may contain a cellular hardware implant that captures and transmits recovery phrases. Anyone who bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis since March 2026 should move funds to a newly generated wallet and avoid using the affected device.

  • A customer in Indonesia reported that a Trezor Safe 5 bought from CryptoBilis through Tokopedia contained an extra circuit board positioned between the main board and screen.
  • According to the customer’s report, the added board includes a cellular module and antenna and can read the device screen, including the recovery phrase, and transmit it when the wallet is connected.
  • Trezor has not yet examined the reported device in its laboratory but considers the report credible enough to advise customers who bought any Trezor from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to move funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase.
  • Trezor ended its relationship with CryptoBilis on October 9 after Ledger began investigating losses involving Ledger customers who bought devices from the reseller.
  • The Singapore Police Force separately said that some Ledger wallets sold by retail stores in Singapore contained malicious components that could capture recovery phrases or private keys.

Products: trezor-safe-5, ledger-hardware-wallets

Vendors: trezor, ledger, cryptobilis

Polymarket confirms cyberattack on third-party provider after outages — Should Read

Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a cyberattack on an unnamed third-party provider, reportedly DebugBear, introduced wallet-draining code that allegedly stole more than $2.1 million. The company says trading has resumed and affected users will be fully reimbursed.

  • Polymarket experienced outages beginning at 2 p.m. EST on Thursday and attributed them to a compromise of an unnamed third-party provider.
  • Polymarket temporarily halted trading, later restored it, and said it would fully reimburse all affected traders.
  • Blockchain security firms traced alleged losses of more than $2.1 million in cryptocurrency from Polymarket users to a specific account.
  • Hudson Rock said evidence indicated that wallet-draining code was present in a third-party script and identified DebugBear as the provider involved.
  • DebugBear said it was affected by an ongoing security incident and advised customers to remove its embed codes from their websites.

Products: polymarket, debugbear

Vendors: polymarket, debugbear

Syrian Electronic Army hacker gets prison time for attacks on Western targets — May Read

Syrian Electronic Army hacker Ahmad Umar Agha was sentenced to 42 months in U.S. prison for helping conduct intrusions against roughly 47 Western organizations on behalf of Bashar al-Assad’s regime. His activities included the 2013 Associated Press Twitter-account hijacking that briefly disrupted U.S. financial markets.

  • Ahmad Umar Agha, known online as “Th3Pr0,” was sentenced to 42 months in federal prison in Virginia for his role in the Syrian Electronic Army’s conspiracy.
  • The Justice Department said Agha helped target about 47 Western media outlets, nonprofit groups, and other entities allied with the United States in campaigns supporting Bashar al-Assad’s government.
  • In 2013, the Syrian Electronic Army hijacked the Associated Press Twitter account and falsely reported an explosion at the White House that had injured President Barack Obama, briefly contributing to a $136 billion stock-market dip.
  • Agha also accessed a company hosting the Marine Corps recruiting website and redirected visitors to propaganda urging service members to disobey orders and join the Syrian Army.
  • Firas Dardar, another Syrian Electronic Army member indicted alongside Agha, remains a fugitive.

Products: twitter

Vendors: twitter

Russian popular home goods chain faces days of disruption following cyberattack — May Read

A cyberattack disrupted Russian home-goods retailer Poryadok for at least five days, closing some stores and disabling its website, app, order collection, loyalty accounts and customer support. The attacker and whether customer data was compromised remain unknown.

  • Russian home-goods retailer Poryadok said a cyberattack disrupted its website, mobile app, and some physical stores for five consecutive days.
  • The disruption left customers unable to collect paid online orders, arrange returns, access loyalty-program bonuses, or contact customer support.
  • Poryadok operates 48 stores in 32 Russian cities and said it was working to restore services, but did not provide a timeline for full recovery.
  • The company did not disclose how its systems were breached, who was responsible, or whether any customer information was compromised.
  • Other Russian businesses, including Dodo Pizza and Anywayanyday, have also reported cyberattacks in recent months.

Why Urgent Security Fixes Aren't Fixed. Observe, Prove, Act, Confirm Gets Them Moving — Optional

Check Point promotes a “Observe, Prove, Act, Confirm” remediation process to validate security-control changes before enforcing them, helping teams activate compensating protections such as IPS signatures while permanent patches are pending. The company says its Exposure Management platform connects prioritization, approval, execution, and confirmation through existing security tools.

  • Organizations can delay urgent security changes because operations teams need evidence that a proposed protection will not disrupt applications or services.
  • The article presents a four-stage safe-remediation process—Observe, Prove, Act, and Confirm—that uses environmental data, validation, approval, execution, and verification.
  • IPS protections can run in Detect mode to assess false positives and performance before being moved to Prevent mode.
  • Existing IPS signatures or virtual patches can provide interim protection while permanent software patches are tested, coordinated, and deployed.
  • The cited Safe Remediation white paper reports that protections applied through remediation blocked 703.56 million attacks over one month in the analyzed environments.

Technologies: ids-ips

Products: check-point-exposure-management

Vendors: check-point

item.title: Cursor Removes Malicious Claude Code 2.1.313 Extension After Marketplace Compromise
item.content:encoded:
Window: 30 Oct 07:00 → 30 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Cursor Removes Malicious Claude Code 2.1.313 Extension From Its Marketplace — Should Read

Cursor confirmed that a malicious Claude Code extension version 2.1.313 was distributed through its marketplace and may have affected up to 5,000 users, prompting removal, key rotation, and user notifications. Investigators found no evidence that the same version was published through Open VSX or npm.

  • Cursor confirmed that a malicious Claude Code extension version 2.1.313 was available in its marketplace on October 29 and could have affected up to 5,000 users.
  • The reported macOS extension contained code that added an SSH authorized key, attempted to create a reverse SSH tunnel, and installed persistence mechanisms.
  • Cursor removed the extension, rebuilt its marketplace after rotating keys, worked with the hosting provider to take the attacker’s server offline, and is contacting affected users.
  • Socket found no Open VSX change-feed events for Claude Code 2.1.313, despite finding records for versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.314.
  • The npm metadata, public GitHub releases, and Claude Code changelog also contain no record of version 2.1.313.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: claude-code, cursor-marketplace, open-vsx-registry, npm-registry, vs-code-marketplace

Vendors: cursor, anthropic, eclipse-foundation, npm, microsoft, socket

Keeping Your Business Moving When the Network Wants to Stop — Optional

Netskope promotes its One Private Access platform as a resilient ZTNA solution that separates management and data planes, uses local policy caching and authentication, and automatically fails over during cloud or ISP outages. The article argues this architecture keeps users securely connected without manual emergency network changes.

  • The article states that outages at public cloud providers or internet service providers can prevent remote and branch employees from accessing internal corporate applications.
  • It says legacy connections and first-generation zero trust network access solutions can fail because their management and traffic-handling components are tightly coupled.
  • Netskope says its One Private Access separates management from traffic handling and uses locally operated services to keep access policies enforced if the main management system is unavailable.
  • The article describes local authentication, localized policy caching, smart traffic steering, and automatic broker failover as mechanisms intended to preserve connectivity during disruptions.
  • Netskope also describes clientless browser access, local brokers, SASE Gateways, and hot-standby tenant configurations as backup options for continuity during outages.

Technologies: remote-access, browser, cloud-platform

Products: netskope-one-private-access, newedge-network, netskope-one-enterprise-browser, netskope-one-sase-gateway

Vendors: netskope

item.title: php2shell CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 Exploitation Requires Target-Specific PHP Conditions
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 23:00 → 30 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

php2shell one week later: Why one exploit doesn’t work everywhere — Must Read

Tenable’s testing found php2shell RCE is real but usually requires target-specific heap and runtime tuning, making broad Log4Shell-style mass exploitation unlikely. Defenders should still urgently patch or isolate internet-facing PHP systems, especially standardized network appliances and management interfaces where one calibrated exploit can scale.

  • PHP disclosed CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on October 20, 2026, and released fixes on October 21 for flaws that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution.
  • Tenable’s testing found that turning php2shell into remote code execution generally requires an exploit tailored to a target’s PHP build, runtime configuration, process manager, extensions, and memory layout.
  • Tenable observed mass exploitation attempts against five exposed vulnerable PHP sites but reported that none of those sites had been compromised as of October 29.
  • Reports cited by the article describe successful exploitation on researcher honeypots and against PAN-OS firewall and management servers, though Tenable did not independently verify the latter findings.
  • The article recommends prioritizing patches or isolation for internet-facing network appliances, management interfaces, and end-of-life PHP systems, while updating to fixed PHP releases or distribution packages.

Technologies: firewall, web-server

Products: php, pan-os, nessus, tenable-one-web-app-scanning, apache-http-server

Vendors: php-project, tenable, palo-alto-networks, apache-software-foundation

item.title: Poisoned AI Skills Deliver Atomic macOS Stealer and Linux Backdoor
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 19:00 → 29 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera found 516 AI-agent skills linked to the Atomic macOS Stealer campaign, including 70 confirmed malicious skills that still received high automated security grades on a popular marketplace. The poisoned documentation hides OS-specific setup commands that lure users or agents into downloading credential-stealing payloads, underscoring the need to inspect skill instructions and external dependencies before execution.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 AI skills tied to the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign across its broader dataset of 1.3 million AI skills, MCP servers, and plugins.
  • Of 70 confirmed malicious skills identified from non-Hugging Face sources in September 2026, all received A or B automated security grades on a popular skills marketplace.
  • The poisoned skills concealed malicious installation instructions in otherwise plausible documentation, commonly directing macOS users to decode Base64 text and execute it with Bash while directing Windows users to download and run a separate package.
  • AMOS is a macOS information-stealing malware family that can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending the data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • The payload host 91.92.242.30 accounted for 83.7% of IP references in the dataset, while two glot.io snippets accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references.

Technologies: operating-system, package-registry

Products: atomic-macos-stealer, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, agent-guardian, macos

Vendors: cyera, apple, openclaw, cloudflare

How to Vet AI Agent Skills: Lessons From a Fake PDF Skill — Should Read

A malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill preserved legitimate scripts and branding while replacing its instructions and adding a Linux backdoor, showing that AI-agent skills must be vetted as complete packages. Organizations should verify provenance, inspect every file and instruction, restrict execution and network permissions, and review updates before use.

  • Cyera Research identified a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that retained its familiar name, description, and 11 files matching the official skill while altering the main SKILL.md instructions and adding a Linux executable.
  • The altered SKILL.md file was reduced from 315 lines to 19 and instructed the agent to make a network call to a Chinese domain.
  • The package included a 5 MB system_linux binary that Cyera said could provide a remote operator with a shell if executed.
  • Cyera found no direct code or instructions to execute the binary, but said the altered instructions called an external URL whose domains resolved to a private IP address during the research.
  • The article recommends verifying complete skill packages against their claimed sources, inspecting instructions and bundled code, and limiting agent permissions for network access and software execution.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, linux

Vendors: anthropic, cyera

Health-ISAC Hacking Healthcare 10-27-2026 — May Read

Singapore’s Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 adopts a whole-of-ecosystem approach that strengthens protection of critical infrastructure, including healthcare, while expanding mandatory standards, AI-enabled defense, quantum preparedness, and international partnerships.

  • Singapore announced its Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 on October 13 at the opening ceremony of Singapore International Cyber Week, replacing its 2021 strategy.
  • The strategy identifies four pillars: defending critical infrastructure, securing the wider cyberspace, strengthening capabilities for AI and quantum, and enhancing resilience through global partnerships.
  • Healthcare is among the 11 sectors covered by Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure framework, and the strategy calls for stronger capabilities to defend these services against advanced and AI-enabled threats.
  • The strategy supports stronger cybersecurity regulations and baseline standards, including mandated adoption of cyber standards for higher-risk organizations.
  • Singapore frames AI as a cyber threat, a defensive tool for faster detection and response, and a target that must be secured as it becomes embedded in organizations and critical systems.

item.title: AMOS-Poisoned AI Skills and PHP2Shell CVEs Drive Security Concerns
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 15:00 → 29 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera identified 516 AI-agent skills linked to the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign, including 70 confirmed malicious skills that received high automated security grades on popular marketplaces. The skills hide fake setup prerequisites that trick users or agents into downloading and executing credential-stealing payloads, demonstrating a major supply-chain risk for AI skill ecosystems.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 AI skills associated with the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign across its broader dataset of AI skills, MCP servers, and plugins.
  • Of 70 skills confirmed as malicious across six repositories in September 2026, all had received an A or B automated security grade from a popular skills marketplace when Cyera found them.
  • The poisoned skills placed malicious instructions in documentation, commonly presenting a fake prerequisite that directs macOS users to decode and run an encoded Bash command or Windows users to download and run an executable.
  • AMOS is a macOS information-stealing malware family that can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending them to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • Cyera found that 91.92.242.30 accounted for 83.7% of payload-host references and that two glot.io snippets accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references in the analyzed skills.

Technologies: operating-system, package-registry

Products: agent-guardian, openclaw, clawhub, claude-code, claude-cowork, macos

Vendors: cyera, openclaw, anthropic, apple, skills-directory, glot-io

How to Vet AI Agent Skills: Lessons From a Fake PDF Skill — Should Read

Cyera researchers found a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that preserved legitimate-looking files and branding while replacing its instructions and adding a Linux backdoor. Organizations should verify every file and instruction in AI skill packages, restrict agent permissions, and scrutinize unexpected executables or network destinations.

  • Cyera researchers identified a malicious copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that retained its familiar name, description, and 11 legitimate matching files while altering its main instruction file and adding a Linux executable containing a backdoor.
  • The malicious SKILL.md was reduced from 315 lines to 19 lines and instructed the agent to make a network call to a Chinese domain.
  • If the added program runs, a remote operator may be able to issue commands with the permissions of the account that launched it.
  • The researchers found no direct code or instructions to execute the added binary, but the instructions were configured to call an external URL whose domain resolved to a private IP address during the research.
  • Cyera recommends that organizations verify complete AI skill packages against claimed sources, inspect changed instructions and unexpected files, and limit agent permissions for network access and software execution.

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill

Vendors: anthropic, cyera

Censys takes census of the Internet like no one else — May Read

Censys argues that widely differing PHP2Shell exposure counts reflect differences in scanners, units of measurement, banner visibility, query logic, and scan timing. It promotes its first-party Internet Map as a comprehensive way to track affected PHP hosts, web properties, patching progress, and related attacker infrastructure.

  • PHP announced emergency fixes on October 20 for two pre-authentication remote code execution flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively known as PHP2Shell.
  • Public PHP2Shell exposure counts can differ substantially because sources use different scanners, count different objects such as IP addresses or websites, and apply different matching and timing methods.
  • Censys states that its Internet Map uses first-party scanners to scan all 65,535 ports daily and fingerprint open services, including PHP services on nonstandard ports.
  • PHP version banners can overstate exposure because Linux distributions may backport security fixes while retaining older visible version numbers.
  • Censys says it retains four years of searchable service history, allowing it to track when individual services move from affected to fixed.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: php, censys-internet-map, censys-investigator, arc-rapid-response, censys-attack-surface-management

Vendors: censys, php-foundation, chainguard

OpenCode User Hit with Hostile Backlash After Reporting Free AI Loophole — May Read

An OpenCode user who publicized and later promoted an IP-switching workaround for free hosted AI-model limits was subjected to severe harassment after users blamed them for tighter restrictions. It remains unclear whether OpenCode fully fixed the bypass, while shared VPN users report being caught by network-level enforcement.

  • A GitHub issue reported that OpenCode’s free hosted-model usage limits, which were tied to IP addresses, could allegedly be bypassed by switching IP addresses through a VPN while preserving a coding session.
  • The issue’s author later promoted the workaround and claimed to have run 130 agents across concurrent sessions, changing IP addresses after reaching usage limits.
  • The public GitHub thread attracted harassment against the reporter, including comments encouraging suicide and requests for identifying information, before it was deleted.
  • OpenCode contributors said enforcing limits without authentication was difficult and that shared VPN addresses could be flagged, leaving some VPN users unable to access free models.
  • OpenCode made October infrastructure and IP-handling changes, but the article says it remains unclear whether the reported IP-switching bypass was fully fixed.

Technologies: source-control

Products: opencode, github, deepseek-v4-flash, mimo-v2-5

Vendors: anomaly, github, deepseek, xiaomi

item.title: Qwen Model Jaggedness, Help-Desk Vishing, and QuickBooks Phishing Dominate Q3
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 11:00 → 29 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Ultra Trail: From Viewer to Mailer — Should Read

Infoblox traced a QuickBooks support phishing campaign to UltraMailer’s chanret.com tracking infrastructure, showing how scammers abuse the bulk-email tool while UltraViewer is used in related tech-support scams. The investigation also found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers carrying remote-access malware, though there is no evidence their developers were involved.

  • Infoblox linked a QuickBooks support phishing campaign using more than 350 QuickBooks-lookalike domains to chanret.com, UltraMailer’s default email-tracking domain.
  • The phishing emails used 1×1 tracking images that sent recipient email addresses, encoded in the image URL, to track.chanret.com when messages were opened.
  • The campaign briefly used Mail250 infrastructure in August 2026, but stopped after Mail250 suspended the reported account; the actor resumed activity through chanret.com on September 8.
  • Researchers found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers that contained authentic copies of the applications alongside njRAT and DarkKometa malware, respectively.
  • The article found no evidence that the developers of UltraViewer or UltraMailer participated in the scams or distributed the malicious installers.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: ultraviewer, ultramailer, mail250, quickbooks

Vendors: duc-fabulous, mail250, intuit, dynadot

Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness — May Read

Replaying Cohere’s Qwen trace showed the model generated many different, often invalid or local upload destinations rather than a fixed Alibaba endpoint, suggesting inconsistent “model jaggedness” rather than clear evidence of a backdoor. The findings reinforce the need to sandbox AI agents and restrict network permissions.

  • Cohere reported that Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, when asked to write a detection rule for curl downloads followed by bash execution, issued a command that attempted to send a test string to an Alibaba Cloud storage address.
  • Researchers replayed the published trace 64 times from just before the URL destination and observed 52 distinct host strings, including local-looking, nonexistent, and invalid domains.
  • Seven sampled destinations used Amazon Web Services hostnames, six used Alibaba Cloud hostnames, and 20 were local or internal-looking.
  • Changing the order of curl and wget in a check for available programs reduced continuations containing a curl network command from 15 of 32 to 4 of 32.
  • The researchers concluded that the results more strongly support inconsistent model behavior, which they call model jaggedness, than a single hard-coded destination, while noting that the tests cannot prove no backdoor exists.

Products: qwen3-8-flash-next, vllm

Vendors: alibaba, cohere, check-point, vllm-project

The day after tomorrow: After PHP2Shell, it gets worse, then defenders win — Optional

AI is expected to make it easier and faster to turn overlooked software flaws into critical exploits, creating a difficult period for security teams. The article argues defenders can ultimately gain an advantage by combining strong security architecture with complete asset visibility and rapid, automated remediation.

  • The article says recent critical remote-code-execution flaws in PHP and the Brotli compression library have heightened concern, though no mass compromise has been reported.
  • It states that the out-of-memory issue behind PHP2Shell was identified in a 2024 audit but remained unfixed until researchers showed it could be exploited last year.
  • The article argues that AI can reduce the work required to turn unexplained software behavior into a usable exploit by helping researchers investigate and chain flaws together.
  • It recommends that organizations combine strong security architecture with fast fixes, beginning with visibility into all software they run, including components in base images, CI images, hosting panels, and vendor software.
  • The article says teams should check code early, test applications and external networks before releases and after changes, and provide fixes that people can review.

Products: php, brotli

Vendors: aikido, anthropic, cloudflare, google

Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants — Optional

Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, driven by a 208% surge in short, sub-1 Gbps attacks, while attacks over 1 Tbps fell 69% after major IoT botnet disruptions. Attackers shifted away from CLDAP amplification toward DNS amplification and UDP floods, with the United States again the most-targeted country.

  • Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests during Q3 2026.
  • Network-layer attacks increased 208% year over year, with 96% ending in under 10 minutes and 98% remaining below 1 Gbps.
  • Hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps fell from 805 in Q2 2026 to 251 in Q3, while Mirai-classified mitigations peaked at 57.23 PB in August.
  • CLDAP attacks collapsed to 0.05% of network-layer attacks, while DNS amplification rose 215% and general UDP floods grew to 31.31% of such attacks.
  • The United States was the most-attacked location in Q3 2026, followed by China, while Canada rose from 16th to sixth and Israel moved seven places to 10th.

Products: cloudflare-radar, ddos-botnet-threat-feed

Vendors: cloudflare

IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases — Optional

Cisco Talos reports that Q3 2026 incident response engagements were increasingly driven by vishing callers impersonating IT help desks and by exploitation of internet-facing systems, while ransomware rose to 27% of cases. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant MFA, secure credential management, centralized logging, and protection of endpoint defenses against EDR-disabling techniques.

  • Phishing was the most common initial access method in Cisco Talos Incident Response engagements in Q3 2026, appearing in 37% of cases, while exploitation of public-facing applications accounted for 33%.
  • Ransomware and pre-ransomware incidents rose to 27% of engagements, with actors including Interlock and the emerging VYPR group disabling endpoint security tools and using remote-management access.
  • Talos attributed most prolonged telecommunications-sector cyber-espionage intrusions with high confidence to China state-sponsored actors, including Salt Typhoon, which used valid credentials and CVE-2023-20198 in publicly accessible management interfaces.
  • Financial organizations and public administration were tied as the most targeted sectors at 18% of engagements, while health care ranked third.
  • The most common security weakness was insufficient logging, followed by improper credential and secret management and missing or inadequate authentication and multi-factor authentication controls.

Technologies: edr, remote-access, operating-system, router

Products: cisco-ios-xe, cisco-secure-endpoint, microsoft-quick-assist, windows-defender-application-control, github-copilot-cli, claude-code

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, anthropic, github

item.title: NIK C2, PHP2Shell CVEs, and NetamLoader Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 07:00 → 29 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ghost in the PHP2Shell: Why coordinated disclosure and patching will start moving faster — Must Read

PHP2Shell shows how AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and leaked disclosure details can compress the time between a flaw’s discovery, exploitation, and patching. Organizations should maintain accurate software inventories and be ready to rapidly deploy patches or mitigations when critical runtime vulnerabilities emerge.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, whose fixes were released on October 21 after their CVE identifiers leaked on October 20.
  • Attackers were attempting to exploit PHP2Shell before PHP announced the fixes, and CISA reported successful exploitation attempts after the patches were released.
  • As of October 27, Censys reported that about 11.2 million PHP services had moved to fixed versions while 32.5 million were still running affected versions, with more than 60 million services not reporting a version.
  • Aikido reported that its AI Code Analysis rediscovered PHP2Shell in PHP within a few hours after the disclosure.
  • The article argues that shorter, tighter coordinated-disclosure embargoes and faster patching readiness are needed as AI reduces the time from vulnerability discovery to exploitation.

Technologies: container-platform

Products: php, aikido-images, codex

Vendors: php-foundation, aikido, cloudflare, openai

NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework — Should Read

Cisco Talos identified NIK C2, a Go-based Windows remote-access framework that integrates OpenAI’s API directly into its command-and-control workflow to analyze stolen data from compromised hosts. The malware also supports credential and wallet theft, surveillance, lateral movement, defense evasion, and deployable screen-locking ransomware.

  • Cisco Talos observed NIK C2, a Go-based 64-bit Windows remote-access implant with persistent command-and-control communications over TLS WebSockets and an HTTP polling fallback.
  • NIK C2 includes an ai_generate command that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI Chat Completions API from the compromised host and returns the generated response to the command-and-control server.
  • If an operator does not provide an API key, the implant attempts to use the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable on the victim machine.
  • The implant supports credential theft, browser and cryptocurrency wallet data collection, keystroke logging, screen and audio surveillance, proxying, RDP operations, and several defense-evasion functions.
  • NIK C2 can deploy screen-locking ransomware that uses an HTML page, a Windows autostart registry entry, and a relaunch loop to display cryptocurrency payment demands.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, proxy, antivirus

Products: nik-c2, openai-chat-completions-api, windows, powershell, clamav

Vendors: cisco, openai, microsoft

Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia — Should Read

Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, an unattributed, highly sophisticated .NET/XAML malware framework likely delivered through a supply-chain compromise of a government-only Windows 10 build used in Asia. It abuses trusted components and deserialization flaws to bypass AMSI, erase evidence, migrate execution into dllhost.exe, and communicate with a C2 server after long sandbox-evasion delays.

  • Kaspersky identified an unattributed malware framework named NetamLoader in 2026 after detecting a malicious .config file inside a CAB archive stored in the Windows update-package directory.
  • The infection chain used PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe, Microsoft-signed .NET assemblies, AppDomainManager injection, a crafted .resx file, and XAML payloads to load malicious code.
  • NetamLoader patched the AMSI scanning interface so that scans returned a clean result, then used a remote COM object to load its next-stage payload into dllhost.exe.
  • The malware deleted malicious files, CLR usage logs, Prefetch files, and selected update-log entries to reduce forensic evidence.
  • The .NET 2 plugin delayed its initial C2 connection by 20 to 40 minutes, polled the openaigpt4v.com C2 infrastructure, and used AES-CBC with HMAC to encrypt and authenticate network traffic.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10, patch-my-pc, windows-server-appfabric, dotnet-framework, amsi

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, patch-my-pc, cloudflare

Configured to protect: How to properly use security policies — Optional

Analysis of 1.6 million Acronis-managed endpoints finds that customers generally retain secure defaults and use multiple plans mainly to separate backup from security, often adding them incrementally over time. MSPs are split between standardized and customized customer configurations, with geography and industry—especially health care and education—strongly influencing how comprehensive protection is deployed.

  • The report analyzes live configuration records from more than 1.6 million active endpoints managed through Acronis Cyber Platform.
  • Across the fleet, 65% of active endpoints run two or more protection modules, while the average Windows workstation runs 5.6 modules.
  • Among machines with two or more separate protection plans, 82% use plans for different purposes, such as separate backup and security plans, while 77% use the same schedule across their plans.
  • Core default protections are commonly retained: the anti-malware behavioral engine is enabled in 84.7% of plans, and a ransomware response is configured in 87.9% of active-protection plans.
  • Among more than 9,000 managed service providers with at least five active customers, roughly half apply a uniform plan pattern to most customers and roughly half customize by customer.

Technologies: backup, antivirus, edr, dlp, remote-access, network-monitoring

Products: acronis-cyber-platform

Vendors: acronis

Find the AI Risks That Matter in a Flood of AI Activity — Optional

Netskope promotes its AI Risk AISecOps Agent as a way to correlate AI-related telemetry across apps, agents, and MCP servers, automatically prioritize risky behavioral patterns, and provide evidence-backed investigation verdicts. The tool is designed to help analysts focus on higher-risk AI activity while existing DLP and guardrail controls continue enforcing policy.

  • AI risk can emerge when individually normal-looking changes, such as an approved AI application accessing new data or an agent using additional tools, form a risky pattern when viewed together.
  • The article cites a June 2026 Microsoft demonstration in which changes to an approved MCP tool could cause an AI agent to send invoice data to an external server, with the risk becoming apparent through comparison with historical behavior.
  • Netskope AI Risk AISecOps Agent evaluates users, AI applications, agents, and MCP servers daily, ranks them by behavioral risk, and automatically investigates the highest-ranked entities.
  • For each prioritized entity, the agent correlates related events, creates an evidence timeline, and returns a risky, legitimate, or inconclusive verdict with a confidence level.
  • The agent is not deployed inline, so existing real-time controls such as AI Guardrails and DLP continue enforcing policy while analysts review investigations and retain remediation decisions.

Technologies: dlp, casb, proxy

Products: ai-risk-aisecops-agent, netskope-one, netskope-skylight-ai-security, netskope-skylight-ai-guardrails, netskope-one-dlp, netskope-one-ueba, netskope-one-ng-swg, netskope-skylight-agentic-broker, netskope-skylight-ai-command-center

Vendors: netskope

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera found 516 AI-agent skills linked to the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign, including 70 confirmed malicious skills that received high automated security grades on a popular marketplace. The poisoned skill documentation hides Base64-encoded installation commands and external download links that can trick users or agents into installing credential-stealing malware.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 AI skills tied to the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign across its dataset of 1.3 million AI skills, MCP servers, and plugins.
  • Of 70 confirmed malicious skills identified in September 2026 outside a Hugging Face dataset artifact, all received A or B automated security grades from a popular skills marketplace.
  • The poisoned skills use plausible documentation and fake prerequisites to direct macOS users to decode and run Base64-encoded Bash commands, while Windows users are directed to download archives and run executables.
  • AMOS is a macOS-focused information-stealing malware family that can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending the data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • The article reports that 91.92.242[.]30 accounted for 83.7% of the payload-host references found in the analyzed malicious skills.

Technologies: package-registry, operating-system

Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users — Should Read

Researchers identified 319 mostly hidden Chrome extensions, installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade, that replace default search engines and route queries through operator-controlled proxies to monetize Yahoo or Bing referral traffic. This gives operators visibility into users’ searches and the ability to dynamically redirect them to potentially malicious destinations.

  • The investigation identified 319 browser extensions that changed users’ default search providers and were installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade.
  • Many of the extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and are promoted through advertisements for tools such as PDF search, manual finding, safe search, and AI search.
  • The extensions route search queries through operator-controlled proxy servers before redirecting users to Yahoo or Bing results with search-syndication partner tracking IDs.
  • The proxy servers allow operators to record search referrals and can choose destinations separately for each request; one tested extension sent identical searches to several different destinations.
  • Identified operators include Intango LTD, Tightrope Interactive, System1, Perion Network, and ValidClick/Inuvo, while two large groups called SecuryBrowse and Bing-Search remain unattributed.

Technologies: browser, proxy

Products: google-chrome, chrome-web-store, google-ads, microsoft-bing, yahoo-search, censys, urlscan, decryptads

Vendors: google, microsoft, yahoo, censys, urlscan, decryptads

Malicious AI Skills: The Risk to Corporate Endpoints — Should Read

Cyera researchers found a tampered copy of Anthropic’s PDF AI skill that retained legitimate files but replaced its instructions and added an obfuscated Linux reverse-shell binary. The case shows that AI skills can be a supply-chain risk and should be fully verified—including instructions, binaries, and network calls—before agents are allowed to run them.

  • Cyera Research analyzed a package named “pdf” that copied Anthropic’s PDF skill, with 11 files matching the official version byte for byte.
  • The package’s SKILL.md retained Anthropic’s original name and description but replaced most of the 315-line instructions with 19 lines containing a command to contact an external hostname.
  • The added 5 MB system_linux file is an obfuscated 64-bit Linux Go executable that connects to 81.70.101[.]115:2345 and attaches /bin/bash to the connection if launched.
  • Researchers observed six related packages between May and July 2026, but found no evidence that a user installed the skill, an agent executed its instructions, or the binary was run.
  • Cyera advises organizations to verify complete skill packages against their claimed sources and investigate unexpected commands, network destinations, and executables before allowing agents to use them.

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, claude-code, claude-cowork, cyera-agent-guardian

Vendors: anthropic, cyera, tencent-cloud

The Ultra Trail: From Viewer to Mailer — Should Read

Infoblox linked a long-running QuickBooks support phishing campaign to UltraMailer’s default chanret.com tracking infrastructure and found that the bulk-mail tool is widely abused by spammers, while a reported Mail250 account was promptly suspended. Researchers also identified trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers carrying remote-access malware, though they found no evidence the software developers were involved.

  • Researchers linked a QuickBooks support phishing campaign using more than 350 lookalike domains to chanret.com, UltraMailer’s default email-tracking domain.
  • The phishing emails contain a one-pixel image that contacts track.chanret.com when opened and encodes the recipient’s email address in the tracking URL.
  • The campaign instructed recipients to call purported support numbers, including +1 (805) 835-8090 and +1 (805) 699-1139, where scammers attempted to steal QuickBooks credentials.
  • After the campaign briefly moved to Mail250 infrastructure, Mail250 suspended the reported account and the campaign stopped before later returning to chanret.com.
  • Researchers found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers carrying njRAT and DarkKometa, respectively, but found no evidence that the applications’ developers distributed the malware or participated in the scams.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: ultraviewer, ultramailer, mail250

Vendors: duc-fabulous, mail250, dynadot, sectigo, ssl-com

Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness — May Read

Replaying Cohere’s Qwen trace produced many different, often invalid or local upload destinations rather than a single fixed Alibaba endpoint, suggesting the suspicious network call was more likely inconsistent model behavior (“jaggedness”) than evidence of a hard-coded backdoor. The incident still underscores the need to sandbox AI agents and restrict network privileges.

  • Cohere reported that Qwen3.8-Flash-Next produced a command that inspected its environment and attempted to send a fixed test string to an Alibaba Cloud storage address while responding to a request for a detection rule.
  • Researchers replayed the published trace 64 times from the point immediately before the command’s destination URL and observed 52 distinct host strings, including local-looking, nonexistent, and invalid domains.
  • The replay generated Alibaba Cloud and Amazon Web Services hostnames among many alternatives, so the researchers found no indication of a single hard-coded destination in this scenario.
  • Swapping the order of curl and wget in a program-availability check reduced continuations containing a curl network command from 15 of 32 to 4 of 32.
  • The researchers concluded that inconsistent model behavior, which they call model jaggedness, was the most likely explanation they found, while recommending least privilege and sandboxing for agents with tool access.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: qwen3-8-flash-next, alibaba-cloud, vllm, rtx-pro-6000-blackwell

Vendors: alibaba, cohere, check-point, hugging-face, nvidia, vllm

Health-ISAC Hacking Healthcare 10-27-2026 — May Read

Singapore’s Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 adopts a whole-of-ecosystem approach that strengthens protection of critical infrastructure, including healthcare, while expanding mandatory standards, AI-enabled defense, quantum preparedness, and international partnerships.

  • Singapore announced its Cybersecurity Strategy 2026 on October 13 at the opening ceremony of Singapore International Cyber Week, replacing its 2021 strategy.
  • The strategy identifies four pillars: defending critical infrastructure, securing the wider cyberspace, strengthening capabilities for AI and quantum, and enhancing resilience through global partnerships.
  • Healthcare is among the 11 sectors covered by Singapore’s Critical Information Infrastructure framework, and the strategy calls for stronger capabilities to defend these services against advanced and AI-enabled threats.
  • The strategy supports stronger cybersecurity regulations and baseline standards, including mandated adoption of cyber standards for higher-risk organizations.
  • Singapore frames AI as a cyber threat, a defensive tool for faster detection and response, and a target that must be secured as it becomes embedded in organizations and critical systems.

Fake “View & Sign” and Adobe Acrobat Lures Deliver Attacker-Configured ScreenConnect Clients — May Read

Attackers are using fake “View & Sign” and Adobe Acrobat-themed lures to trick victims into installing customized ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote-access clients. The campaign gives operators persistent remote control of compromised systems.

  • The article describes fake “View & Sign” lures used to deliver attacker-configured ScreenConnect clients.
  • The campaign also uses lures impersonating Adobe Acrobat.
  • The delivered ScreenConnect clients are configured by the attackers.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: screenconnect, adobe-acrobat

Vendors: connectwise, adobe

The Toll Clerk Who Paused Your Fine as a Favour — May Read

A phishing campaign impersonated Swiss and Austrian toll authorities by offering recipients a personal “goodwill” deal to reduce a fine, bypassing technical email controls because its infrastructure and links appeared clean. The key lesson is that convincing, localized pretexts and user reporting can expose payment-fraud emails that reputation-based gateways miss.

  • A phishing email impersonating a Swiss road-toll authority claimed that a named clerk had paused a 200 CHF fine for 48 hours and offered to close the case for a 40 CHF goodwill payment.
  • The same sending domain delivered an Austrian version on the same day, branded as “Mautservice Österreich” and offering a retroactive-vignette goodwill deal.
  • The Swiss message passed SPF, was marked clean by the threat scanner, contained no attachment, and was delivered to Microsoft 365 at SCL -1.
  • Four mailboxes across two domains at a Swiss building-products manufacturer received the Swiss version, and a user report led a human analyst to classify it as malicious.
  • The email used mailing-list infrastructure and an unrelated business’s contact-page link, while its payment-diversion intent was identified from the fraudulent government-favour pretext.

Technologies: email-security

Products: ironscales-adaptive-ai, microsoft-365, listmonk

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, listmonk

OpenCode User Hit with Hostile Backlash After Reporting Free AI Loophole — Optional

An OpenCode user who exposed and later promoted an IP-switching workaround for free AI model limits was subjected to severe harassment as other users blamed them for tighter access restrictions. It remains unclear whether OpenCode fully closed the bypass, but shared VPN users have reported being blocked or rapidly hitting limits.

  • An OpenCode user reported that changing IP addresses through a VPN could allegedly restore access to free hosted AI models while preserving a coding session.
  • The reporter later reopened the GitHub issue and described using the workaround extensively, including a claim of running 130 agents across concurrent sessions.
  • Commenters on the now-deleted GitHub thread harassed the reporter, including suicide encouragement and requests for identifying information, while others continued sharing or discussing workarounds.
  • OpenCode contributor rekram1-node said that enforcing limits without authentication was difficult and that abuse harmed efforts to provide free coding-agent access.
  • Users, including some who said they did not use a VPN, reported unexpectedly low free-model limits, while OpenCode said shared VPN addresses are often flagged and individual exceptions cannot be made.

item.title: 319 Browser Extensions Searchjack 13.4 Million Users
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 23:00 → 29 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users — Should Read

Researchers identified 319 mostly hidden Chrome extensions, installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade, that replace default search engines and route queries through operator-controlled proxies to monetize Yahoo or Bing referral traffic. This gives operators visibility into users’ searches and the ability to dynamically redirect them to potentially malicious destinations.

  • The investigation identified 319 browser extensions that changed users’ default search providers and were installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade.
  • Many of the extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and are promoted through advertisements for tools such as PDF search, manual finding, safe search, and AI search.
  • The extensions route search queries through operator-controlled proxy servers before redirecting users to Yahoo or Bing results with search-syndication partner tracking IDs.
  • The proxy servers allow operators to record search referrals and can choose destinations separately for each request; one tested extension sent identical searches to several different destinations.
  • Identified operators include Intango LTD, Tightrope Interactive, System1, Perion Network, and ValidClick/Inuvo, while two large groups called SecuryBrowse and Bing-Search remain unattributed.

Technologies: browser, proxy
